rows.context: Questions retrospectively unified life stories and examines trajectories across changing social fields. Institutional naming and the interview situation help produce the unity being narrated; this does not rule out every life history.

strands.title: Narrated unity and relational trajectories
strands.focus: Bourdieu asks how institutions, interviews and retrospective storytelling produce coherent selves, and proposes trajectories within changing fields. Life history remains possible under relational scrutiny.

strands.title: Scale, norms and bounded agency
strands.focus: Levi distinguishes several uses of lives and locates choices within conflicting norms. Group coherence becomes a question to investigate, not an automatic starting assumption.

rows.context: Studies embodied dispositions, improvisation and the power involved in classification.
rows.works: Outline of a Theory of Practice (1972; English 1977); Distinction (1979)

strands.title: Habitus and social position
strands.focus: Durable dispositions allow improvisation; neither mechanical obedience nor unconstrained choice.
strands.works: Outline of a Theory of Practice; Distinction

strands.title: Classification and power
strands.focus: Bourdieu critically expands Durkheim’s cognitive account toward social power.

strands.title: Historical classifications and their uses
strands.focus: Bourdieu relates practical classifications to social positions and struggles over recognition. He uses Duby’s three-orders analysis as an example; Vickery later uses Bourdieu in a different historical inquiry.

rows.context: Relates tastes and cultural practices to social position; a specific resource alongside other approaches to goods.

strands.title: Taste and social position
strands.focus: Read tastes and cultural practices in relation to social position, alongside approaches centered on circulation or household provisioning.
